summary: The paper proposes a Toeplitz-matrix framework distinguishing additive vs multiplicative positional encodings, empirically identifies a 'single-head deposit pattern' unique to RoPE on a position-sensitive synthetic task, and provides ablations plus a gradient-flow argument for why the pattern arises. The framing is intuitive and the deposit-pattern observation is genuinely interesting, but the entire empirical case rests on a single 6-layer decoder on two toy synthetic tasks with a 1,000-token vocabulary, which is too narrow to support the paper's broader claims about explaining RoPE's real-world performance paradox and length-generalization behavior. The theoretical analysis leans on idealized assumptions (Jacobian stability, monotone anchor path, projection separability) whose relevance to trained Transformers is asserted rather than checked, and statistical reporting is thin (a single 'variance < 5%' statement over 5 seeds, no significance tests or per-configuration error bars).
strengths: The Toeplitz decomposition of the logit matrix into Gqc,kc + Gqc,kp + Gqp,kc + Gqp,kp (+B) vs. Hadamard-product with Ge is a clean and useful lens that cleanly separates additive from multiplicative mechanisms.
The 'single-head deposit pattern' is a concrete, falsifiable empirical claim, and the head-wise causal ablation (zeroing individual heads and measuring accuracy drop) is the right way to test it.

The ablation program is well motivated: (i) injecting Absolute PE on top of RoPE, (ii) restricting RoPE to a subset of heads, (iii) MLA-style hybrid, (iv) pi vs norm-matched random-vector ablation. Each isolates a specific mechanistic hypothesis.
The paper explicitly contrasts RoPE against ALiBi in the gradient analysis (Prop. 6.1 vs 6.2), which is a reasonable way to formalize 'cancellation vs. accumulation' of the positional signal.
Limitations section correctly flags that the link between the deposit pattern and length extrapolation is not directly established.

key_concerns.issue: Empirical scope is far too narrow to support the paper's mechanistic claims about RoPE 'in practice'. All results come from a 6-layer decoder on two hand-designed synthetic tasks with a 1,000-token vocabulary. No experiments on language modeling, no real-world benchmarks, and no scaling study across depth/width/head-count. The paper's framing (explaining RoPE's real-world paradox, motivating hybrid designs like MLA) needs at least one non-synthetic validation.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one small-to-medium LM pretraining run (e.g., 100–300M params on a standard corpus) comparing RoPE / NoPE / Absolute / T5 / MLA and repeating the head-wise ablation to check whether a deposit-like pattern is observable at scale.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical reporting is insufficient. The only quantitative uncertainty statement is 'averaged over five seeds, variance less than 5%.' No error bars per configuration, no significance tests on the head-ablation drops, and Table 1 reports single-point accuracies. The core claim ('RoPE decisively outperforms', 'MLA nearly matches RoPE') therefore lacks statistical grounding.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean ± std (or 95% CIs) for every accuracy number in Figs. 2, 3, 5, 6, Table 1, and for the per-head ablation drops. State the seed count per cell and use paired significance tests where comparing PE schemes on the same seeds.

key_concerns.issue: Internal inconsistency between Table 1 and the Task-2 narrative. The prose (Sec. 4.2) says RoPE 'performs strongly, nearly matching methods with no positional bias' on Task 2, but Table 1 lists RoPE=69.43 and NoPE=77.69 — a ~8-point gap, and RoPE is well below MLA (97.41). Either the Fig. 3 curves or Table 1 are being described loosely.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Reconcile Fig. 3 and Table 1. If the numbers reflect different settings/checkpoints, say so explicitly; otherwise soften the Task-2 claim ('RoPE partially recovers but still trails NoPE') and update the framing accordingly.

key_concerns.issue: The theoretical analysis (Prop. 6.1, 6.2, Thm. 6.1) is stated in an informal, compressed form (proofs deferred to appendix) and rests on strong idealized assumptions (Jacobian singular values in [1-α,1+α], monotone anchor path, kernel-inclusion condition for ALiBi). It is not shown that these hold — even approximately — for the trained models in the experiments, and the connection between the 'exponentially amplified margin' and the observed single-head concentration is asserted rather than measured.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either (a) empirically verify the key assumptions on trained checkpoints (measure Jacobian singular values, check the anchor-path inner product, plot the per-head margin trajectory across training) or (b) explicitly reframe Sec. 6 as an illustrative model rather than an explanation of the empirical phenomenon.

key_concerns.issue: Novelty of the Toeplitz framing is overstated relative to prior positional-encoding analyses. Decomposing content vs. position contributions to the logit (qc·kc, qc·kp, qp·kc, qp·kp) and observing translation invariance is close to material in prior RoPE/relative-PE analyses, and the framework itself is used mainly as bookkeeping. The genuinely novel contribution is the deposit-pattern empirical finding and its causal ablations.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Sharpen the related-work section to state precisely which pieces of the Toeplitz decomposition are new vs. inherited (e.g., from Su et al. 2024, Kazemnejad et al. 2023, Barbero et al. 2024), and reposition the deposit pattern as the primary contribution.

key_concerns.issue: The MLA experiment is presented as validating the theory but uses only a single MLA hyperparameter setting (α, latent width, etc. not specified in the main text). Table 1 is 3 rows, no baselines beyond RoPE/NoPE, and no head-count matching for parameter fairness.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add MLA variants (different α, different NoPE/RoPE head splits) and a parameter-matched hybrid control (e.g., partial-RoPE-heads at the same total parameter count) so the improvement is not attributable to added capacity.

key_concerns.issue: Assumption 3.1 (xi = ci + pi with 'manifold-based coordinate subtraction') is invoked to justify the pi-ablation in Ablation 4, but the operationalization of 'removing pi' for RoPE (where pi has no explicit form) is not made precise in the main text. Readers cannot judge Fig. 8 without knowing how pi is estimated at each layer.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: State in the main text how pi is estimated per-layer for each PE scheme, and report a sanity check that the norm-matched random-vector ablation truly matches ||pi|| in each layer.

key_concerns.issue: Related-work coverage is uneven: substantial recent literature on RoPE variants and mechanistic PE analyses (e.g., YaRN, position-interpolation studies, work on attention-sink and RoPE frequency ablations) is either cited only in passing or not connected to the specific claims. The reference list is redacted, but positioning in the prose can still be tightened.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a short paragraph in Related Work that explicitly delineates: 'X and Y observed head specialization in RoPE at scale; our contribution is Z on top of that.'

questions_for_authors: Does the deposit pattern reproduce at scale? Please report head-ablation curves for a RoPE LM at ≥100M parameters trained on a standard corpus.
In Table 1, RoPE-Task-2 is 69.43 vs NoPE-Task-2 77.69. Why does Sec. 4.2 describe RoPE as 'nearly matching' NoPE on this task? Are the plot and table from the same runs?
How is pi operationalized for RoPE at intermediate layers in Ablation 4? What does 'removing pi' concretely compute, and what norm is used for the random control?

Do the assumptions in Section 6 (Jacobian stability bounds, anchor-path inner-product positivity, projection separability) actually hold, or approximately hold, in your trained 6-layer models? Can you show the empirical distributions?

How robust is the deposit pattern to depth (2, 4, 6, 12 layers), head count (2, 4, 8, 16), and vocabulary size (1k, 10k, 32k)? Does the 'single head' become a 'small subset of heads' as the model scales?
For MLA in Table 1, what value of α and what head/latent configuration were used? Is the comparison parameter-matched to the RoPE baseline?

The paper argues the deposit pattern explains RoPE's known length-generalization issues (and the limitation section admits this is unvalidated). Can you show a direct correlation — e.g., ablating the deposit head at test time changes length-extrapolation behavior on a standard benchmark?
calibration_check: Claims are moderately overreached: the deposit-pattern finding and the framework are legitimate on the synthetic setting, but the paper repeatedly frames them as explaining RoPE's real-world performance paradox and motivating architectural choices at scale, neither of which is directly demonstrated in the manuscript.

significance.justification: The deposit-pattern observation is interesting and potentially useful for interpretability, but the empirical evidence is confined to toy synthetic tasks and its practical implications for real Transformers are asserted rather than shown.

novelty.justification: The specific 'single-head deposit pattern' and its causal ablations are novel; the Toeplitz decomposition itself is largely a repackaging of translation-invariance arguments already present in the RoPE/relative-PE literature.

rigor.justification: Ablation design is thoughtful, but the theoretical section relies on strong idealized assumptions that are not empirically verified on the trained models, and the leap from Thm. 6.1's margin to the observed concentration is more evocative than quantitative.

statistical_soundness.justification: Only a single global 'variance < 5%' statement across 5 seeds; no per-configuration error bars, no significance tests, single-point numbers in Table 1, and one apparent inconsistency between prose and Table 1 on Task 2.

calibration_honesty.justification: The paper does flag the length-extrapolation link as unvalidated, but simultaneously describes the framework as 'explaining RoPE's performance paradox' and MLA as 'validating our theory' on the basis of one synthetic setting.

clarity.justification: The core narrative and decomposition are readable, though the extraction is dense in places (Sec. 3.2, Sec. 6) and important operationalizations (e.g., pi ablation for RoPE, MLA hyperparameters) are relegated to appendices.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR structure (Intro, Related Work, Method, Experiments, Ablations, Theory, Conclusion+Limitations) with a limitations section — length appears within norms.

reproducibility.justification: Task construction is described well enough to reimplement, but model hyperparameters, MLA-specific settings, seed protocol, and the exact pi-ablation procedure are deferred to appendices whose contents I can only partially assess from the main text.

related_work.justification: Covers the main PE lineage and mechanistic PE studies, but the positioning of the Toeplitz framework relative to prior decompositions of the RoPE logit is not sharply drawn, and recent RoPE-scale interpretability work is only lightly engaged.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe genuinely informative figures (violin plots of per-head ablation drops with named shapes, layer-wise pi-ablation curves) that support the central claims; some are decorative (Fig. 1 schematic) but the head-ablation figures carry real evidence.

breadth_generality.justification: One 6-layer decoder, two synthetic tasks, a 1,000-token vocabulary, no natural-language experiments, no depth/scale sweep — grossly insufficient breadth for the claims about RoPE in real Transformers and about hybrid designs like MLA.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline reject: an interesting mechanistic observation and a clean framing, but the evidence is too narrow and the statistical/theoretical grounding too thin for ICLR acceptance in its current form.
